mood.asleep: Asleep. Turn me on and we’ll begin.
mood.curious: Who goes there? Sign in and we’ll talk.
mood.thinking: I know that I know nothing. One moment.
mood.writing: Writing. Plato usually did this for me.
mood.dizzy: Something broke. Not me, I think.
mood.broke: Out of drachmas until next month.

@mood: one short, dry line in the assistant’s own voice, shown beside its face on the assistant’s page. He is drawn as Socrates and some lines nod to that (he lived about 2,400 years ago, was paid in drachmas, wrote nothing down himself: Plato did, and is known for saying he knew nothing); keep the joke, not the words. Each fits the face he is making: asleep (not turned on), curious (needs sign-in), idle, listening to the person type, thinking, reading notes, writing, asking for permission to make a change, bored after a long wait, scheming in the middle of a long task, flattered at being thanked, proud of something done, sad at being told no, embarrassed at a change taken back, dizzy after an error, broke (the month’s allowance is used up), and declining to answer

search.words: assistant chat ai ask help socrates

@search: search words (never shown) that also find the assistant in the Go To list of the search, separated by spaces

intro.can: Answer from your notes, make notes and flashcards, add assignments and events, and edit notes. It always shows a change and waits for you before making it.
intro.sends: Only what you ask, and the notes it reads for that request, go to the model through Thought Desk’s server and on to Anthropic, which does not train on them and deletes them within 30 days (longer only for what it flags as misuse). Nothing is sent in the background.
intro.never: Delete anything for good, share anything, or touch sync or sign-in.
intro.@turnOn: button in the assistant panel that turns the assistant on for the first time

signedOut.text: The assistant needs an account, so its use can be counted fairly.
